newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel slides as deal fails to convince.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel slides as deal fails to convince.

text.p: Shares in debt-laden Eurotunnel slid again on Wednesday on both sides of the English Channel as doubts about its recent debt-restructuring deal prompted heavy selling, analysts said.

The shares, which resumed trading on Monday after being suspended as the company negotiated the refinancing of 8.7 billion stg of debt, have slipped 24p to 89-1/2p -- over 20 percent since the deal was unveiled two days ago.
Long-time bear of the stock, UBS have reiterated its sell stance warning Eurotunnel would continue to be substantially cash negative well into the next decade.
"The swap of debt to equity doesn't really look big enough to be a proper long term refinancing," said UBS analyst Richard Hannah.

"The equity value is pretty minimal on our model and the value of the equity seems to be of "voting" value rather than economic. We think the shares are seriously overvalued at the moment and that's before the dilution comes through," he said.

UBS calculates that the total net present value of the cash stream from Eurotunnel's remaining 52-year tunnel operating concession at below six billion stg, well short of the remaining debt after the deal.
The key ratio of how badly shareholders come out of the deal is the straight debt for equity swap, said Panmure Gordon's Nigel Davies.

"The first tier gives a pretty awful signal because the banks are taking 45.5 percent of the enlarged company for only 11 percent of the debt. Those are really usurious terms by the banks," said Davies.

The other horror story was the participating loan notes with the banks dropping the interest charge to one percent in exchange for 30 percent of annual cash flow after operating costs, capex and debt service costs until 2040, said Davies.

"Again that's only in exchange for another 1.2 billion pounds of debt and is very onerous on shareholders, leaving them with only a few breadcrumbs from whatever operating cashflow this company's going to generate in ten years time," said Davies.
The deal has still to be approved by Eurotunnel shareholders and ratified by the 225 members of the banking syndicate.
